text:
Nikita Kucherov has asked for a trade, and he's playing like a man who wants every team to see what they'd get. Six points in two games, a dominant run through the rumors, and the rumor mill tossing around Toronto, Montreal and New Jersey as landing spots. As Daily Faceoff put it, he keeps giving the Lightning everything on the ice. How long that arrangement lasts is the biggest question in Tampa.

For now it's working. Tampa Bay is 13-5-2 with 28 points and the process to back it: 55% of all expected goals (the quality of chances) and 56% at five on five, with results and chances agreeing closely. Our playoff odds sit at 94% and the division is close to a coin flip. The 8-3 rout in Buffalo showed what this lineup does when it gets rolling.

The setback is Brayden Point, on injured reserve. His line with Kucherov and Jake Guentzel had outscored teams 8-2. That opened the door for Sam O'Reilly, the two-time Memorial Cup champion, who picked up his first NHL point in his debut.

The depth is a quiet strength. Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev have outscored teams 10-4, and Ryan McDonagh with Erik Cernak is 14-5 with 61% of the chances. John Carlson, paired with J.J. Moser, has fit in. What we'd watch: the Kucherov talks, because a deal would change both the Lightning and whoever gets him.
